title: Billable Hours & Fee Calculation
problem: Lawyers spend significant time calculating billable hours, applying different rates for different tasks, and reconciling time entries against retainers. Manual calculation leads to underbilling or overbilling, both of which damage client relationships. Errors in fee calculations can trigger bar complaints and malpractice claims.
who: Solo practitioners and small firm attorneys without dedicated billing staff

skill_spec.name: Legal Fee Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates total billable fees from time entries with blended rates, retainer deductions, and expense allocation

inputs.name: time_entries
inputs.label: Time entries (task: hours, one per line)

skill_spec.formula_hint: gross_fees = sum(hours * rate per entry), discount = gross_fees * discount_pct / 100, net_fees = gross_fees - discount + expenses, amount_due = max(0, net_fees - retainer_balance), retainer_remaining = max(0, retainer_balance - net_fees)

example_queries: I billed 12.5 hours at $350/hr with a 10% client discount. What's the total fee?
Calculate my invoice: 3 hours research at $300, 5 hours drafting at $350, 2 hours court at $400, retainer balance is $2,000

title: Statute of Limitations Lookup
problem: Lawyers must constantly verify statutes of limitations across different jurisdictions and claim types. Missing a SOL deadline is one of the top causes of legal malpractice claims. Each state has different limitation periods for contracts, torts, fraud, and specialized claims, making manual tracking error-prone.
who: Litigation attorneys, personal injury lawyers, solo practitioners

skill_spec.name: Statute of Limitations Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Instant lookup of statutes of limitations by state, claim type, and special circumstances
skill_spec.data_domain: Statutes of limitations for all 50 states plus federal claims

example_queries: What is the statute of limitations for breach of written contract in California?
SOL for medical malpractice in New York with discovery rule?
How long do I have to file a fraud claim in Texas?

title: IOLTA Trust Account Reconciliation
problem: Lawyers holding client funds must maintain IOLTA trust accounts with strict monthly reconciliation requirements. Errors in trust accounting - commingling funds, overdrafts, or misallocation - can result in disbarment and criminal charges. Manual reconciliation across multiple client matters is tedious and high-stakes.
who: Solo practitioners, small firm managing partners, any attorney handling client funds

skill_spec.name: IOLTA Trust Account Reconciler
skill_spec.one_liner: Reconciles client trust account balances against bank statements and flags discrepancies

inputs.name: client_ledgers
inputs.label: Client ledger balances (client: amount, one per line)

skill_spec.formula_hint: adjusted_bank = bank_balance + outstanding_deposits - outstanding_checks - bank_fees + interest_earned, discrepancy = adjusted_bank - total_client_balances, reconciled = discrepancy == 0, warn if any client ledger < 0 or if bank_fees deducted from trust

example_queries: Bank balance is $45,230. Client ledgers: Smith $12,000, Jones $18,500, Davis $14,730. Outstanding check $500. Is my trust account reconciled?
Reconcile my IOLTA: bank says $100,000, I have 5 client matters totaling $98,500, pending deposit of $2,000, bank fee of $25

title: Engagement Letter Drafting
problem: Every new client matter requires a detailed engagement letter specifying scope, fees, billing practices, and terms. Lawyers spend 30-60 minutes per letter customizing terms for different practice areas. Poor engagement letters lead to fee disputes and malpractice exposure.
who: All practicing attorneys, especially solo and small firm lawyers

skill_spec.name: Engagement Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates customized client engagement letters with proper fee structures and ethical disclosures

variables.name: fee_type
variables.label: Fee arrangement (hourly, flat fee, contingency, hybrid)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Header with firm info -> Client identification -> Scope of representation -> Fee arrangement details -> Billing practices -> Retainer terms -> Client responsibilities -> Termination provisions -> Conflict waiver (if applicable) -> State-specific disclosures -> Signature blocks

example_queries: Generate an engagement letter for a personal injury contingency case in Florida, 33% fee
I need an engagement letter for corporate M&A advisory at $450/hour with a $10,000 retainer

title: Court Filing Deadline Calculator
problem: Lawyers must calculate precise filing deadlines based on triggering events, court rules, and jurisdiction-specific counting methods. Federal and state rules differ on how weekends, holidays, and service methods affect deadlines. Missing a deadline is the #1 cause of malpractice claims, and manual calculation is error-prone.

skill_spec.name: Court Deadline Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates filing deadlines based on triggering event, rule period, service method, and jurisdiction-specific counting rules

outputs.name: safe_deadline
outputs.label: Recommended safe filing date (2 days before)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Start counting day after triggering event. For periods < 11 days (federal), exclude weekends/holidays. Add 3 days for mail service (FRCP 6(d)), 0 for electronic. If deadline falls on weekend/holiday, move to next business day. Federal holidays per 5 USC 6103.

example_queries: I was served a complaint on March 15, 2026 by mail in federal court. When is my answer due?
Calculate the deadline for a 30-day response period starting April 1 in California state court, served electronically

title: Conflict of Interest Check Procedure
problem: Before taking on any new client or matter, lawyers must conduct thorough conflict checks across all current and former clients, adverse parties, and related entities. Failure to identify conflicts violates Model Rules 1.7-1.10 and can lead to disqualification, malpractice liability, and disciplinary action. Solo and small firms often lack systematic procedures.
who: All practicing attorneys, especially solo and small firm lawyers without conflict-check software

skill_spec.name: Conflict of Interest Check Procedure
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step conflict checking procedure compliant with ABA Model Rules 1.7-1.10
steps: Step 1: Identify all parties to the new matter (client, adverse parties, related entities, subsidiaries, affiliates)
Step 2: Identify all attorneys and staff who may work on the matter
Step 3: Search current client database for name matches and variations
Step 4: Search former client database for name matches and variations
Step 5: Check adverse party lists across all open matters
Step 6: Check for business/financial relationships with any party
Step 7: Check for family/personal relationships with any party
Step 8: Review for positional conflicts (taking contrary legal positions in different cases)
Step 9: If potential conflict found - analyze under Rule 1.7 (current client) or 1.9 (former client)
Step 10: Determine if conflict is consentable under Rule 1.7(b)
Step 11: If consentable - prepare informed consent letter with full disclosure
Step 12: Obtain written consent from all affected clients
Step 13: Document the conflict check results and file in matter record
Step 14: If conflict is non-consentable - decline representation
warnings: Warning: Imputed disqualification (Rule 1.10) extends conflicts to all firm attorneys
Warning: Some conflicts cannot be waived even with client consent
Warning: Government attorney conflicts have special rules (Rule 1.11)
Warning: Lateral hire conflicts require screening procedures

example_queries: Walk me through a conflict check for a new divorce client whose spouse is represented by my former colleague
How do I check for conflicts when a new corporate client has subsidiaries I might have dealt with before?

title: CLE Requirement Tracking
problem: Every state has different CLE (Continuing Legal Education) requirements - different total hours, ethics hours, specialty credits, and reporting periods. Lawyers admitted in multiple jurisdictions must track separate requirements simultaneously. Failure to complete CLE results in suspension of license.
who: All licensed attorneys, especially those admitted in multiple states

skill_spec.name: CLE Requirements by State
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of CLE requirements by state including total hours, ethics hours, reporting periods, and special requirements
skill_spec.data_domain: CLE requirements for all 50 states and DC

data_hints.source_law: State bar CLE rules and regulations

example_queries: What are the CLE requirements for California and New York?
How many ethics hours do I need in Texas? When is the reporting deadline?
I'm newly admitted in Illinois - are there additional CLE requirements for new lawyers?

title: Contingency Fee & Settlement Distribution
problem: Personal injury and plaintiff attorneys must accurately calculate contingency fee splits, lien reductions, and net client recovery from settlements. Errors lead to bar complaints, malpractice claims, and trust account violations. Calculations involve fee percentages that may change at different stages, medical liens, costs, and subrogation claims.

skill_spec.name: Settlement Distribution Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates attorney fees, cost deductions, lien payments, and net client recovery from settlement proceeds
skill_spec.formula_hint: If costs from gross: attorney_fee = (settlement - costs) * pct OR settlement * pct depending on agreement. Typical: fee = settlement * contingency_pct, then deduct costs, then deduct liens. net_to_client = settlement - attorney_fee - costs - liens. Always verify net_to_client > 0.

example_queries: Settlement is $500,000 at 33%, I advanced $15,000 in costs, medical liens are $45,000. What does the client get?
Calculate distribution on a $1.2M settlement, 40% contingency post-filing, $50K costs from gross, $120K in liens

title: Legal Memorandum Drafting
problem: Attorneys draft internal legal memoranda to analyze legal issues, predict outcomes, and advise clients. Each memo requires structured analysis (IRAC/CREAC format), proper citation, and balanced discussion of authorities. Junior associates spend 8-15 hours per memo, and quality varies significantly.
who: Junior and mid-level associates, solo practitioners

skill_spec.name: Legal Memorandum Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates structured legal memoranda in IRAC format with proper issue framing, rule statements, and analysis
skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (To, From, Date, Re) -> Question(s) Presented -> Brief Answer -> Statement of Facts -> Discussion (IRAC for each issue: Issue -> Rule -> Application -> Conclusion) -> Overall Conclusion -> Recommendations

example_queries: Draft a memo analyzing whether my client's non-compete clause is enforceable in California
I need a legal memo on premises liability for a slip-and-fall at a grocery store in Georgia

title: Ethics & Disciplinary Risk Advisor
problem: Lawyers face complex ethical situations daily - potential conflicts, dual representation, fee disputes, social media conduct, AI use in practice. Missteps lead to bar complaints, public reprimand, suspension, or disbarment. The 2026 landscape adds new complexities around AI disclosure requirements and emerging regulations.
who: All practicing attorneys, especially solo practitioners without firm ethics counsel

skill_spec.name: Legal Ethics Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Analyzes ethical dilemmas under ABA Model Rules and state-specific rules with risk assessment and recommended actions
skill_spec.expertise_area: Legal ethics, professional responsibility, bar disciplinary rules, AI in legal practice compliance

example_queries: A prospective client told me details about their case before I ran a conflict check, and now I found a conflict. What do I do?
Can I use AI to draft a brief without disclosing it to the court? What are the 2026 rules?
My former client's new matter is adversarial to a current client. Is this a conflict under Rule 1.9?

title: Discovery Response Checklist
problem: Responding to discovery requests (interrogatories, document requests, requests for admission) involves multiple procedural steps, objection deadlines, privilege review, and meet-and-confer requirements. Missing steps or deadlines can result in sanctions, adverse inferences, or waiver of objections.

skill_spec.name: Discovery Response Procedure
skill_spec.one_liner: Complete step-by-step procedure for responding to written discovery requests under federal and state rules
steps: Step 1: Calendar the response deadline (30 days federal/varies state) from date of service
Step 2: Determine service method and calculate any additional time (FRCP 6(d))
Step 3: Review each request individually for scope, relevance, and proportionality
Step 4: Identify proper objections (privilege, work product, overbroad, unduly burdensome, relevance)
Step 5: Draft objections - preserve all objections even if also providing responsive information
Step 6: Conduct reasonable search for responsive documents and information
Step 7: Review documents for privilege - create privilege log
Step 8: Prepare responses to interrogatories (verify under oath)
Step 9: Organize document production with Bates numbering
Step 10: Client review and verification of interrogatory answers
Step 11: Meet and confer on disputed requests before filing motions
Step 12: Serve responses and production within deadline
Step 13: Retain copies of all served responses and document production
Step 14: Calendar supplementation obligations (FRCP 26(e))
warnings: Warning: Failure to timely object waives most objections
Warning: Interrogatory answers must be verified under oath by the party
Warning: Inadvertent privilege disclosure - invoke clawback under FRE 502(b) immediately
Warning: ESI preservation obligations begin when litigation is reasonably anticipated

example_queries: I received interrogatories and document requests in federal court 5 days ago. Walk me through the response process.
What's my checklist for responding to requests for admission? Can I object to some?

title: Malpractice Risk Assessment
problem: Lawyers need to identify and mitigate malpractice exposure in real-time. The top causes of claims are administrative errors (deadlines), inadequate investigation, failure to know the law, planning errors, and inadequate discovery. Most attorneys lack a systematic way to evaluate their risk on active matters.
who: All practicing attorneys, especially solo and small firm lawyers

skill_spec.name: Malpractice Risk Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Evaluates malpractice risk on active matters and recommends preventive actions based on common claim patterns
skill_spec.expertise_area: Legal malpractice prevention, risk management, professional liability

example_queries: I'm handling a complex commercial litigation solo - what are my biggest malpractice risks?
I missed sending a demand letter before the SOL. What are my options and exposure?
What malpractice prevention steps should I take for a contingency fee personal injury case?

title: Settlement Agreement Drafting
problem: Settlement agreements must be comprehensive, covering releases, indemnification, confidentiality, payment terms, and tax implications. Incomplete or ambiguous settlement agreements lead to post-settlement disputes, enforcement actions, and malpractice claims. Each practice area has specific required provisions.
who: Litigation attorneys, mediators, personal injury lawyers, employment lawyers

skill_spec.name: Settlement Agreement Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates comprehensive settlement agreements with appropriate releases, payment terms, and practice-area-specific provisions
skill_spec.structure_hint: Recitals -> Definitions -> Settlement payment terms -> General release of claims -> Carve-outs from release -> Confidentiality provisions -> Non-disparagement -> Tax provisions (1099 reporting) -> Representations and warranties -> Indemnification -> Dismissal with prejudice stipulation -> Governing law -> Entire agreement -> Signature blocks -> Notarization (if required)

example_queries: Draft a settlement agreement for a $250,000 employment discrimination case in New York with confidentiality
I need a PI settlement agreement for $150K structured payment over 3 years in Texas
